scope: Existing staging testnet Router and Signing Worker; six existing wallet objects; no new resources.
method: Each lookup arm sends 36 authenticated requests. Each request makes three sequential no-op object calls. Three objects per role, three rounds, alternating reused and fresh stubs. Signing Worker requests traverse the existing Router service binding.
clock: Date.now spans surround the object fetch and response-body read. These are application spans, not isolated network clocks.
limitations: No-op probes omit protocol execution, persisted reads/writes, and production payload sizes.
The first probe after each deployment includes possible object reconstruction and provider routing work. These effects cannot be separated.
Different arms reuse the same objects and may retain provider routing caches.
Warm means the same object instance answered a preceding probe in this arm, not a guaranteed production condition.
Application clocks do not account for uninterrupted CPU execution. Provider CPU measures whole invocations.
This experiment does not measure Yao setup or establish a signing latency improvement.
Physical execution locations and provider-internal routing are not directly observed.
Samples are sequential and small. They do not establish a population percentile.

conclusion.demonstrated: Warm no-op calls to the same object remain fast across separate incoming requests, fresh handles, APAC hints, and named lookups.
conclusion.notDemonstrated: The experiment does not explain the repeated ~0.5 second dispatch spans in real registration or show a Yao latency improvement.
conclusion.decision: Keep the existing placement and lookup implementation. Do not add a global stub cache or rewrite coordinator placement from these results.
conclusion.nextStep: Correlate actual startup, claim, and package-delivery requests for the same wallet. Record execution-location observations separately from timing. Measure payload sizes and response-header/body-read boundaries before choosing another optimization.

verificationNotes: All captured invocation versions match each arm. Durable Object tails are incomplete; returned instance counters verify all 324 successful calls.
Each object reports exactly one instance and consecutive calls 1 through 18 in each arm.
All three local E2E runs verify unauthorized rejection, unknown-object rejection, fresh handles, service forwarding, and object reuse across requests.
The first hosted attempt was rejected by Cloudflare error 1010 before reaching the Workers. Exact versions were restored. The successful run used the benchmark browser User-Agent.
One read-only D1 query supplied existing wallet ownership metadata for deriving object names. No-op handlers perform no storage calls.
